questions.title: Nth Fibonacci Number
questions.description:
Fibonacci numbers are the hello-world of dynamic programming: each value is the sum of the two before it, so naive recursion explodes into exponential time while memoisation keeps it linear. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long fibonacci(int n)

With fibonacci(0) = 0 and fibonacci(1) = 1, it must return the n-th Fibonacci number. You may write additional static helpers. Use long so large results are not truncated.

Input Format:
One line: n.

Output Format:
One line with fibonacci(n).

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 40

questions.title: Coin Change Combinations
questions.description:
Counting how many ways a set of coin denominations can express an amount (order irrelevant) is the unbounded-knapsack counting DP: extend the amount axis coin by coin so combinations are never double-counted as permutations. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long coinCombinations(int amount, int[] coins)

Each coin may be used any number of times; it must return the number of distinct combinations that total exactly amount.

Input Format:
Line 1: amount A and coin count C. Line 2: C distinct coin denominations.

Output Format:
One line with the number of combinations.

Constraints:
1 <= amount <= 250, 1 <= C <= 10, 1 <= coin <= 250

questions.title: Climbing Stairs Count
questions.description:
You are climbing a staircase with n steps and can climb either 1 or 2 steps at a time. The number of distinct ways to reach the top follows the same recurrence as Fibonacci — the classic warm-up for counting DP, solved with two rolling variables. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long climbStairs(int n)

It must return the number of distinct orderings of 1-step and 2-step climbs that reach step n.

Input Format:
One line: n.

Output Format:
One line with the number of ways.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 40

questions.title: Tribonacci Number
questions.description:
The Tribonacci sequence extends Fibonacci: every term is the sum of the previous three. Computing it with three rolling variables is the canonical memory-optimisation drill — O(1) space instead of a full table. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long tribonacci(int n)

With tribonacci(0) = 0, tribonacci(1) = 1 and tribonacci(2) = 1, it must return the n-th term.

Input Format:
One line: n.

Output Format:
One line with tribonacci(n).

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 30

questions.title: Pascal Triangle Cell
questions.description:
Pascal's triangle is a DP table in disguise: each cell is the sum of the two cells above it. Building it row by row (bottom-up tabulation) yields any binomial coefficient without ever computing a factorial. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long pascalCell(int n, int k)

It must return the value in row n, position k (both 0-indexed).

Input Format:
One line: n k.

Output Format:
One line with the cell value.

Constraints:
0 <= k <= n <= 30

questions.title: Frog Jump Energy
questions.description:
A frog crosses a river by hopping across stones. From a stone it may jump to the next stone or skip one ahead, and each jump costs energy equal to the absolute height difference between the two stones. The cheapest plan is textbook tabulation: the best cost to reach stone i comes from stone i-1 or i-2. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int frogMinEnergy(int[] heights)

It must return the minimum total energy to travel from the first stone to the last (0 when there is only one stone).

Input Format:
Line 1: N. Line 2: N space-separated stone heights.

Output Format:
One line with the minimum total energy.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 30, 0 <= height <= 100000

questions.title: Git Diff Similarity
questions.description:
A code-review tool scores how similar two source files are by the length of their longest common subsequence — the longest run of characters both files share in the same order (gaps allowed). The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int lcsLength(String a, String b)

It must return the length of the longest common subsequence of the two strings (not necessarily contiguous).

Input Format:
Two lines: string a, then string b.

Output Format:
One line with the LCS length.

Constraints:
1 <= |a|, |b| <= 50

questions.title: Truck Load Split
questions.description:
A dispatch office wonders whether a delivery truck with capacity target kg can be filled exactly using some subset of today's parcels. This feasibility question is the boolean core of 0/1 knapsack: one pass per parcel over a rolling boolean table. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int subsetSumExists(int target, int[] items)

It must return 1 when some subset of the item weights sums exactly to target, otherwise 0.

Input Format:
Line 1: target T and item count N. Line 2: N item weights.

Output Format:
One line with 1 or 0.

Constraints:
1 <= T <= 500, 1 <= N <= 25, 1 <= weight <= 500

questions.title: Toll Booth Staircase
questions.description:
A mountain staircase charges a toll on every platform. A maintenance robot may climb 1 or 2 platforms at a time and may start on platform 0 or platform 1; it pays the toll of every platform it stands on. Reaching the top (one step past the last platform) at minimum cost is the min-cost climbing stairs DP. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int minToll(int[] cost)

It must return the minimum total toll to get past the last platform.

Input Format:
Line 1: N. Line 2: N platform tolls.

Output Format:
One line with the minimum total toll.

Constraints:
2 <= N <= 30, 1 <= toll <= 1000

questions.title: Rabbit Colony Growth
questions.description:
A wildlife park models its rabbit colony with a simple recurrence: the colony in month n equals the colony of month n-1 plus twice the colony of month n-2 (each pair from two months ago spawns two new pairs). Starting from colonySize(1) = 2 and colonySize(2) = 3, the numbers explode quickly — memoise and use long. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long colonySize(int month)

It must return the colony size in the given month. You may write additional static helpers.

Input Format:
One line: month.

Output Format:
One line with the colony size.

Constraints:
1 <= month <= 30

questions.title: Cloud Storage Knapsack
questions.description:
A cloud provider packs customer workloads onto one server with a fixed memory budget: each workload has a memory footprint and a price, and every workload is taken whole or not at all. Maximising price under the memory budget is the classic 0/1 knapsack, solved with a rolling 1-D table. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int knapsack(int capacity, int[] weights, int[] values)

It must return the maximum total value of a subset whose weights sum to at most capacity.

Input Format:
Line 1: capacity W and item count N. Line 2: N weights. Line 3: N values.

Output Format:
One line with the maximum total value.

Constraints:
1 <= W <= 500, 1 <= N <= 50, 1 <= weight <= 500, 1 <= value <= 1000

questions.title: Vending Machine Payout
questions.description:
A vending machine must dispense exactly amount credits using the fewest coins from its arbitrary, non-standard denominations (a 1-credit coin is NOT guaranteed to exist). Greedy fails on such systems; bottom-up tabulation over every amount is the reliable answer. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int minCoins(int amount, int[] coins)

Each denomination has unlimited supply. It must return the minimum number of coins, or -1 when the amount cannot be paid.

Input Format:
Line 1: amount A and denomination count C. Line 2: C coin values.

Output Format:
One line with the minimum coin count, or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= A <= 500, 1 <= C <= 15, 1 <= coin <= 1000

questions.title: Gallery Thief Loot
questions.description:
A thief tours a gallery corridor of display cases laid out in a row; alarms connect adjacent cases, so robbing two neighbouring cases triggers a lock-down. Maximising the loot under the no-two-adjacent rule is the house robber recurrence. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long maxLoot(int[] valuables)

It must return the maximum total value that can be taken without choosing two adjacent cases. You may write additional static helpers.

Input Format:
Line 1: N. Line 2: N case values.

Output Format:
One line with the maximum loot.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 40, 0 <= value <= 1000000

questions.title: Autocorrect Edit Cost
questions.description:
An autocorrect engine ranks suggestions by edit distance — the minimum number of insertions, deletions and replacements that turn one word into another. The Wagner–Fischer tabulation fills a two-dimensional DP table over prefixes. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int editDistance(String a, String b)

It must return the Levenshtein distance between the two words.

Input Format:
Two lines: word a, then word b.

Output Format:
One line with the edit distance.

Constraints:
1 <= |a|, |b| <= 50

questions.title: Rod Cutting Profit
questions.description:
A steel workshop buys one rod of length n and may cut it into any whole-length pieces; a piece of length i sells for price[i]. Maximising revenue is unbounded knapsack in disguise: extend the table over lengths, trying every first cut. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int rodProfit(int n, int[] price)

price has n+1 entries with price[0] unused and price[i] the price of a piece of length i (1 <= i <= n). It must return the maximum revenue for the whole rod.

Input Format:
Line 1: N. Line 2: N prices — price[1] through price[n].

Output Format:
One line with the maximum revenue.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 30, 1 <= price <= 1000

questions.title: DNA Motif Match
questions.description:
A genome lab compares two DNA reads for their longest common contiguous motif — a substring both share exactly, in place. Unlike LCS the match must be unbroken, so a broken diagonal in the DP table resets to zero. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int longestCommonRun(String a, String b)

It must return the length of the longest common contiguous substring.

Input Format:
Two lines: string a, then string b.

Output Format:
One line with the longest common run length.

Constraints:
1 <= |a|, |b| <= 50

questions.title: Rising Stock Streak
questions.description:
An analyst scans a stock's daily closes for the longest strictly increasing streak of days (values must rise across the chosen subsequence — order fixed, gaps allowed). The O(n^2) tabulation keeps, for every day, the best streak ending there. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int lisLength(int[] values)

It must return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.

Input Format:
Line 1: N. Line 2: N closing prices.

Output Format:
One line with the LIS length.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 100, -1000000000 <= price <= 1000000000

questions.title: Robot Grid Routes
questions.description:
A warehouse robot starts at the top-left cell of a storage grid and must reach the bottom-right cell, moving only right or down; shelving units (blocked cells marked 1) can never be entered. Counting its route options is a 2-D tabulation with blocked cells zeroed out — route counts grow fast, so answer in long. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long countRoutes(int[][] grid)

grid holds R rows of C cells (1 = blocked, 0 = open). It must return the number of distinct routes (0 when start or end is blocked).

Input Format:
Line 1: R C. Then R lines with C space-separated cells.

Output Format:
One line with the number of routes.

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 15, each cell is 0 or 1
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= R, C <= 15, each cell is 0 or 1

questions.title: Emergency Supply Path
questions.description:
Disaster relief: each cell of a damage grid carries a supply cost, and a courier must walk from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell moving only right or down, paying every cell it enters. The cheapest route is the classic minimum path sum tabulation. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int minPathSum(int[][] grid)

It must return the smallest total cost of any right/down route from (0,0) to (R-1,C-1).

Input Format:
Line 1: R C. Then R lines with C space-separated costs.

Output Format:
One line with the minimum path cost.

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 15, 1 <= cost <= 1000

questions.title: Budget Combo Count
questions.description:
A finance team reviews expense items and asks: in how many distinct ways can a target budget be hit exactly by some subset of the items? Counting subset sums is the counting twin of 0/1 knapsack — one pass per item over a rolling table, each item used at most once. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long countSubsets(int target, int[] values)

It must return the number of subsets of values whose elements sum exactly to target.

Input Format:
Line 1: target T and item count N. Line 2: N item values.

Output Format:
One line with the number of subsets.

Constraints:
1 <= T <= 500, 1 <= N <= 25, 1 <= value <= 500
